newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ keen to wrap up Ansett Australia deal.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ keen to wrap up Ansett Australia deal.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd on Wednesday welcomed Australian government approval of its proposed purchase of 50 percent of airline Ansett Australia and said it hoped to quickly wrap up the deal.

"Some work is required now to put appropriate arrangements in place, but the welcome announcement from the Australian government will enable us to consummate the deal very quickly after it is submitted for formal approval at an extraordinary general meeting of Air New Zealand's shareholders on September 27," managing director Jim McCrea said.
He said he was confident approval would be forthcoming.

McCrea added: "The conditions attached to the approval -- particularly as they relate to ownership and control arrangements for the Ansett Australia international airline operation -- appear acceptable and workable from our perspective."
Air NZ is buying the half-stake from TNT Ltd, but the Australian government said that the New Zealand airline should not be allowed to take 50 percent of Ansett's international operations.
Ansett International Ltd (AIL) will be 51 percent owned by an Australian holding company, Holdco, and 49 percent by Ansett. Holdco will be 100 percent Australian-owned.
Air NZ is investing a total A$475 million to buy into Ansett, using a cash issue, new borrowings and existing cash reserves.
